title: SummitScale QBR: Inference Health & Growth Strategy Review
topics: Actionable next steps for pilot expansion
summary: Quarterly health review focused on steep usage growth in recommendations pipeline, cost anomalies tied to peak-hour tail, and proposal for a blended Dedicated+Hosted routing strategy. Agreed to run a focused 2-week burst pilot using Dedicated reserved pools and KV-cache tuning; Redwood to share pricing matrix and a short benchmark plan. Security docs and updated SLA to be shared with procurement.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Owen (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Liam (SummitScale VP Eng), Jaya (ML Platform), Marcus (SRE), Sofia (Product), Tom (Finance)

Summary: Quarterly check-in on inference health, cost drivers, and a proposal to run a dedicated burst pilot.

[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick roll call — I see Liam, Jaya, Marcus, Sofia, Tom — awesome. We'll tee up usage and costs, then Owen has a short technical deep dive, and we close with pilot next steps.

[00:28] Liam O'Connor (SummitScale): Hey Maya, thanks. We're a little tight on time on the customer side, but we want to get through the major blockers — we've been seeing higher-than-expected spend on recommendations during peak windows.

[00:40] Priya Singh (Redwood): Noted. We'll focus on the tail costs and the routing options.

[00:52] Owen Ramirez (Redwood SE): I'll start with a quick snapshot — we pulled token-level traces for the last 60 days, looked at sequence length distribution, and there are these four spikes around 09:00, 13:00, 20:00 UTC that line up with feed refreshes. Those spikes correlate with higher latency and token multipliers due to repeated full-context prompts.

[01:20] Jaya Patel (SummitScale): Right — those are our batch refreshes for the recommendations cache. We didn't realize each refresh was rehydrating full history. The KV cache behaviour is... it's not exactly what we thought. Sometimes it's not hit as often as we'd expect.

[01:40] Marcus Hill (SRE): For us it's an ops issue too — during spikes we see concurrency climb and then fallback to hosted lower-tier models which blows up token count and cost. We want to avoid that noisy neighbor effect.

[02:05] Maya Chen (Redwood): That's exactly the scenario where Dedicated burst capacity helps: you reserve a pool to absorb those peaks and configure smart routing policies so high-priority traffic pins to Dedicated and non-critical flows go to hosted. The blended approach reduces the tail cost while keeping overall utilization efficient.

[02:35] Sofia Alvarez (Product): Quick question — does the blended routing change our model outputs or quality? We can't have different versions returning different recommendation distributions.

[02:50] Owen Ramirez (Redwood SE): Good callout. The runtime supports consistent model version pinning across environments; when we route, we can either route to the same model binary that's deployed to Dedicated or use a verified compatible variant. There can be slight variance if you switch quantization profiles, but we can lock quantization to avoid distribution drift.

[03:20] Tom Becker (Finance): The spend impact — can you give us rough delta numbers if we go 2-week pilot with 30% of peak traffic on Dedicated? We need to show execs a payback window.

[03:33] Maya Chen (Redwood): We'll put a short model — Owen, are you able to pull a quick back-of-envelope?

[03:39] Owen Ramirez (Redwood SE): Yeah. Using their last 30-day peak traces: if we route 30% of peak window traffic to Dedicated with reserved capacity and enable prefix/KV caching, we estimate a 22–28% reduction in per-token bill for those windows, with a one-time onboarding/benchmarking cost. Net over the month that's approximately 9–12% total reduction. I'll convert that into a spreadsheet.

[04:10] Liam O'Connor (SummitScale): That's helpful. We care about regressions too — can the Redwood Console give us drift alerts when quality degrades post-rollout?

[04:25] Priya Singh (Redwood CSM): Yes — we can wire up the Quality monitors to your prompt set. We'll run before/after evals and set up regression alerts on the console. We'll need a canonical prompt set from you.

[04:42] Jaya Patel (SummitScale): We'll share a representative set — maybe 300 prompts covering long history cases. Also, what about SLOs? We need P95 latency under 120ms on critical endpoints.

[04:55] Owen Ramirez (Redwood SE): For P95 120ms, Dedicated on our GPU pool with tuned batching and KV caching is achievable for the bulk of your distribution. For corner cases with very long contexts we may hit slightly higher, but we can set fallback flow that still meets functional correctness albeit slightly higher latency. We'll put together a test harness for P50/P95/P99.

[05:25] Marcus Hill (SRE): On security — procurement asked to see SOC two, our legal team will need encryption details (KMS/HSM), and for private deployments we might need a hybrid VPC. Can Redwood support a VPC private control plane?

[05:40] Maya Chen (Redwood): Absolutely. For Private we offer customer-managed networking, KMS integrations, and audit logs. We'll pass the SOC 2 pack and the HSM/KMS matrix. Priya will add procurement to the thread.

[05:55] Tom Becker (Finance): Any differences in billing cadence between Dedicated reserved contracts versus hosted? We need monthly forecasting alignment.

[06:05] Maya Chen (Redwood): Dedicated has a reservation component (monthly/annual commit) plus variable usage for burst. We can model a burst-only short pilot as a temporary reserved pool with credits applied — we'll include line items in the pricing sheet.

[06:20] Sofia Alvarez (Product): Are there known gotchas when moving from hosted to dedicated that have tripped other customers? We want to avoid surprises.

[06:30] Owen Ramirez (Redwood SE): A few things: model variant mismatch at different quant levels, unexpected tokenization differences for multi-lingual prompts, and cache warm-up — during the first 24–48 hours you often see higher cost until prefix/KV cache warms. We recommend synthetic warm-up runs during the pilot.

[06:55] Jaya Patel (SummitScale): That warm-up is important. Can we do a simulated warm-up with replayed traffic?

[07:05] Owen Ramirez (Redwood SE): Yes, replay is standard — we can replay anonymized traces to warm the caches and validate latency. We'll provide scripts and a small harness.

[07:20] Maya Chen (Redwood): Okay, quick demo from Owen on what the dashboard will show for the pilot — token-level cost, P95 latency, KV-hit rate, and model variant consistency.

[07:32] Owen Ramirez (Redwood SE): (screen share tone) So on the Console, you'll see per-route breakdowns, route-level toggles for Dedicated pinning, and a cost tab that maps token cost to model variant. Note there's an events stream where we annotate rollouts and fallbacks. Also, your team can attach evaluation suites to routes and baseline quality.

[08:05] (short silence, typing)

[08:20] Liam O'Connor (SummitScale): The Console trace looks good. For the pilot we'd like to measure: avg token cost, P95 latency, KV-hit rate, and quality regression on the 300-prompt set. If those look good we can expand.

[08:33] Priya Singh (Redwood CSM): Perfect. We'll align the measurement criteria in the pilot doc.

[08:40] Marcus Hill (SRE): A question on fallbacks: if Dedicated capacity is saturated and we fallback to hosted, can we enforce a strict model quality guardrail so we don't degrade the customer experience?

[08:54] Owen Ramirez (Redwood SE): Yes — you can set automatic fallback policies with either (a) a compatible model that preserves output distribution or (b) deny/queue requests. Most customers choose a compatible variant plus graceful degradation.

[09:10] Jaya Patel (SummitScale): For the 2-week pilot, what instrumentation do you need from us? Logs, traces, prompt sets?

[09:18] Priya Singh (Redwood CSM): We'll need the prompt set, a tokenization sample, and access to a read-only S3 with anonymized traces or a CSV of latencies. Owen will share the exact schema.

[09:30] Tom Becker (Finance): Any penalties if we exceed committed burst? We need to evaluate cost risk.

[09:38] Maya Chen (Redwood): For short pilots we usually use a capped burst model with overage rates spelled out in the pilot contract. We'll include caps and alerts so you never get surprised.

[09:50] Sofia Alvarez (Product): Is there anything else we should be aware of from the roadmap side? Are there new runtime features that will affect our decision in the next quarter?

[10:02] Owen Ramirez (Redwood SE): We're rolling out tiered KV eviction and better cross-tenant cache isolation in Q3, which reduces noisy neighbour risk, and a new kernel selector that improves long-context throughput. None of that should block a pilot; rather it should improve economics mid-pilot.

[10:28] Jaya Patel (SummitScale): Good to hear. A couple of procurement items: updated SLA, data residency options for EU traffic, and proof of encryption in transit at our interconnect.

[10:40] Maya Chen (Redwood): We'll drop the SOC2 package and an addendum that outlines EU routing and encryption details.

[10:50] (brief cross talk about calendar invites)

[11:05] Maya Chen (Redwood): Let's capture agreed pilot scope: 2 weeks, target the three daily peak windows, 30% of peak routed to Dedicated, measures: avg token cost, P95 latency under 120ms, KV-hit rate target > 70%, and zero material quality regressions. Any objections?

[11:27] Liam O'Connor (SummitScale): Sounds reasonable. We'll sign off provided the pricing model matches the spreadsheet.

[11:35] Tom Becker (Finance): I'll review once you share the detailed numbers.

[11:42] Jaya Patel (SummitScale): We'll prepare the prompt set and a sample of trace data, aim to have it by Friday.

[11:50] Maya Chen (Redwood): Action items — I'll email the pricing spreadsheet and pilot contract template. Owen will send test harness and warm-up scripts. Priya will schedule the kickoff and include SRE and procurement.

[12:05] Marcus Hill (SRE): One final ops note — please include an escalation path and pager contacts in the pilot doc, we need an on-call for the first 48 hours.

[12:12] Priya Singh (Redwood CSM): Will do.

[12:20] Sofia Alvarez (Product): Thanks, everyone. Looking forward to the pilot.

[12:25] Maya Chen (Redwood): Great — we'll follow up with the materials. Thanks all.

Meeting end.
